title: Davis uses DIA deputization to get access to the crash retrieval program

tellings.quote: using my security clearances my need to know my access including my letter that I'm deputized by Jim Lowsky as a representative of the of the Defense Intelligence Agency. I used all that leverage and authority to get into the crash retrieval program. I couldn't get access to CCraft bodies or talk to the people, but I was able to get in to the people who handled all of that at a programmatic level and got confirmation that all of that was real, that all of it happened.

plain: A Pentagon scientist named Eric Davis says that from around 2008 he used his security clearances and a letter from an official named Jim Lacatski, which named him a representative of the Defense Intelligence Agency, the US military's intelligence service, to get into what he calls the crash retrieval program, a secret effort to recover crashed craft. Davis says he could not see the craft or bodies, or talk to the people who work with them, but he did reach the people who run it at the programme level. He says they told him all of it was real and all of it happened, which, if true, would mean the US government holds crashed craft that are not human-made.
